title: Book 3 — Thalia, Chapter 115
paragraphs: These, then, are the extremities in Asia and Libya. But as to the extremities of Europe towards the West, I am not able to speak with certainty. I do not accept the tale that there is a river called Eridanos in barbarian speech, flowing into the sea that lies towards the north wind, from which amber is said to come; nor do I know of any real existence of “Tin Islands” from which tin comes to us. For first, the name Eridanos itself is Hellenic and not barbarian, and was invented by some poet; and second, though I took pains to discover it, I have not been able to hear from any eyewitness that there is a sea on the other side of Europe. However that may be, tin and amber certainly do come to us from the extremity of Europe.
